convoLines.text: "What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I hate to ask this, but I can't shake it. I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Can you do anything?"
"The fever's not breaking and I'm barely keeping food down. I need help — real help, not just water."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Carmen owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"I keep turning over the last thing Carmen said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I'm keeping a photo of someone I left behind. I haven't told anyone. Simple as that."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Norman shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I've got things to see to. Don't be a stranger."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Teresa doesn't wait for an answer. "We need to discuss how things are run here."
Teresa has an edge today — something curdled.
"Murkcap — The gills begin to breathe — a sweet, wrong smell rolls out from under the cap. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"Ha." Not amused. "I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. I keep my head down. Old habit. It kept me alive before; it keeps me alive now. There. You happy?"
"Never mind the sickness I'm fighting — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "I dreamed Carmen was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said there was something you regretted. You didn't want to get into it. I won't ask. Just — are you carrying it any lighter?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Norman shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"The pantry's nearly bare. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know the sweet manioc patch past the treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
They nod. "Okay."

"It's my son, Hisashi. Asked if the taken ones were bad. I said no. He asked if they were boring. I did not answer. The pods get into my sleep some nights. Row on row of them, humming like a held note -- and I wake up reaching for something that isn't there."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "You saw it too, right? Duel. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"I'll tell you plain — Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«我什么都听不懂。什么都不懂！»
«对，对，没错。» (you catch '对' — right/yes) They nod back, slowly.
«你真是太好了，谢谢你。» (you catch '太好了' — too kind) A grin breaks through, quick and warm. "Fuck you."
«我不会忘记的。» You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «你有吃的吗？» (you catch '吃的' — food)

Dong tilts their head. "...What?" You try again, slower, redder. A long beat. Then the smallest smile. "是真的。," they say — perfectly. "You meant." They knew all along; they just wanted to watch you work for it.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What do you make of all this? Really."
"Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not. You'd know about that."
"Still on what you make of all this."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Since Norman died... I keep expecting to see Norman at the fire. Stupid."
"I sleep with one ear uncovered, always. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"The fire feels smaller without Norman. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"And... scene. Good talk."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«这是什么地方？我们在哪儿？» (What place is this? Where are we? — you're fairly sure)
«没错，你说得对。» (Right, you're correct. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly.
«你是个好人。» (You're a good person. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm. "Shit."
«谢谢。真的，谢谢。» (Thank you. Truly, thank you. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «晚上睡哪儿？» (Where to sleep at night? — you're fairly sure)
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Do you dream about before? Or is it all — this — now?"
"Then it's not gone. Not really. Keep going back."
"Still on what you dream about. You'll see."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You want to know what I did in the raid? I stood down Inspiration at the treeline — it ran. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"I keep touching the spot where it grazed me. Like it'll explain itself."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d8: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Carmen Heo is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d8: 🕯️ Carmen Heo is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d9: That night, they bring Carmen home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d8: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d8: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."

d8: ◈ SYSTEM: "RATINGS DIP. The audience wants STAKES — pointed ones. A PALISADE. Stockpile 14,000 kcal, 350 wood and 60 stone. Walls make such good television. You will thank us when the teeth come."
d8: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
d8: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 35. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 3."
d8: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d9: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
d9: SYSTEM: Quest protocol integrated. Objectives will appear.
d9: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 40. I've been watching what you're becoming, little living. Names for your shelf: Beard Moss, Rain Dancer. What they DO — that's still yours to learn."
d9: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
d10: ◈ SYSTEM: "Ooh. NEIGHBORS. You know what neighbors are for? STORYLINES. Go knock — worst case, it's CONTENT. Best case? The show gets BIGGER."

d10: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.
d10: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 50. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 4."
d10: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
burialWindowSay: d8: The Highbeam Deer thrashes its antlers at you — getting close has a price.

d8: The Highbeam Deer thrashes its antlers at Norman — getting close has a price.
d9: That night, they bring Carmen home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d10: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+6 integration)
d11: You say a few words for Carmen. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d11: You bury Carmen. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d11: "Carmen owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d11: "I keep turning over the last thing Carmen said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d15: "Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "I dreamed Carmen was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
echoV2Sample: d11: The village raises a marker by the fire — Carmen, day 11. the wild. A place to stand.
echoV2DeltaSample: d11: The village raises a marker by the fire — Carmen, day 11. the wild. A place to stand.
halfRationLines: d46: "Triage tents and broth for the sick, or half rations till it passes, or the healthy hunt hard to keep everyone fed. Pick — everything costs."
